formulas.formula: Catch every write-off, keep the receipts and see what it saves you.
Setup: your name, the year, a rough tax rate, the IRS mileage rate and when to flag missing receipts.
Deductions: every business cost. Business % for things you also use personally (like your phone).
Mileage: business trips. Tick Round trip to double the miles.
Home Office: your office size and home costs. It compares both IRS methods and picks the bigger one.
Summary, Missing Receipts and Dashboard total it up by category and quarter.
Business meals are usually 50% deductible. The Meals category halves them for you.
Check the IRS rate for your tax year and type it in Setup.
Keep proof for every cost, especially anything over $75 and all travel.
A tracker to stay organized. Your tax pro has the final word.
Red = missing receipt or a typo.

=IF(R4=0,"Log your first business expense to start.",IF(R9>0,R9&IF(R9=1," receipt is"," receipts are")&" missing. See the Missing Receipts tab.","Every big expense has a receipt. You are audit-ready."))
Income tax + 15.3% self-employment tax. Used to estimate savings.
Use the IRS rate for this tax year.
Missing receipts above this amount are listed.
Blank Business % = 100%. Meals are counted at 50% automatically.

=IF(TRIM(C{row}&"")="",0,IFERROR(MATCH(LOWER(TRIM(C{row}&"")),{"advertising & marketing","bank & payment fees","car & truck (parking, tolls)","contract labor","education & training","equipment","insurance (business)","legal & professional","meals (50%)","office supplies","phone & internet","rent (office or studio)","repairs","software & subscriptions","supplies & materials","taxes & licenses","travel","utilities (business)","health insurance (self-employed)","retirement contributions","other"},0),21))
Business driving only (not your commute). Miles one way; tick Round trip to double it.
Only a space used regularly and only for work counts. Yearly home costs go in the white cells.
Simplified = $5 per sq ft, up to 300 sq ft. Regular = your share of real home costs (more records needed).
